en.title: Google really is a saint!
en.summary:
Google really is a saint!!

There’s a free tool many people don’t know about: Google Colab!
The interface seemed daunting at first, but after a little digging, it really opens up a new world!!

The free tier gives you a cloud NVIDIA T4 with 16GB of VRAM!
There’s so much you can do with it!

1. Mount Google Drive to store files.
2. Run open-source LLMs: deploy Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek and other models directly to try local inference.
3. AI image generation: run open-source models like Stable Diffusion and SDXL.
4. AI audio: use Whisper for speech-to-text and run open-source TTS models to generate voiceovers.
5. AI video: test video generation, video enhancement, super-resolution and other models.
6. Model fine-tuning…

en.title: Google really is a saint!
en.summary:
Google really is a saint!!

There’s a free tool many people don’t know about: Google Colab!
The interface seemed daunting at first, but after a little digging, it really opens up a new world!!

The free tier gives you a cloud NVIDIA T4 with 16GB of VRAM!
There’s so much you can do with it!

1. Mount Google Drive to store files.
2. Run open-source LLMs: deploy Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek and other models directly to try local inference.
3. AI image generation: run open-source models like Stable Diffusion and SDXL.
4. AI audio: use Whisper for speech-to-text and run open-source TTS models to generate voiceovers.
5. AI video: test video generation, video enhancement, super-resolution and other models.
6. Model fine-tuning…
en.reason: Free Google Colab provides a cloud NVIDIA T4 with 16GB VRAM for mounting Google Drive, running Qwen, Llama and DeepSeek, generating images with Stable Diffusion or SDXL, transcribing with Whisper, TTS, and model fine-tuning.

en.title: Top AI labs are turning into "talent black holes" — Claude Code team engineer gives first interview since leaving
en.summary:
Don't overinflate the halo around top AI labs."
"Don't overinflate the halo around top AI labs."
Word count: 5,830
Reading time: about 19 minutes
Three core Claude Code members have left Anthropic in the past two weeks: product lead Cat Wu joined OpenAI, while engineer Thariq Shihipar and desktop lead Anthony Morris also departed. In a podcast after leaving, Thariq reflected on the career path from startups to top AI labs.
The Claude Code team lost core members three times in just over ten days; Cat Wu moved to core product management at OpenAI; Thariq went from a multimillion-dollar game startup to an AI lab and deep involvement in Claude Code development.
Recommended for AI product leads, technical leads of large-model engineering teams, and CTOs of AI startups.
Translation: Lin Qibei
Editor: Cai Fangfang

en.reason: Anthropic lost three Claude Code core members within about two weeks, including product lead Cat Wu to OpenAI, as departing engineer Thariq Shihipar reflects on top AI labs’ talent-black-hole pull after shuttering a game startup that raised $10 million.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: Google Research的AI仅凭智能手表脉搏与运动传感器筛查高血压，在196人研究中检出率65.8%，高于传统诊室测量的55.3%，该功能已进入Google Health app但仍不能替代正式诊断。

en.reason: Google Research's cuff-free AI flags high blood pressure from a smartwatch's pulse and motion sensors alone, detecting 65.8% of cases in a 196-person study versus 55.3% for traditional in-office measurement, and it's already live in the Google Health app while not replacing formal diagnosis.

sources.title: AI 生成视频何时才能告别“抽卡”？藏在高效生成背后的返工与成本难题
sources.title_zh: AI 生成视频何时才能告别“抽卡”？藏在高效生成背后的返工与成本难题
sources.title_original: AI 生成视频何时才能告别“抽卡”？藏在高效生成背后的返工与成本难题
sources.summary:
多模态AI加速内容创作，距离一次成型还有多远？
多模态AI加速内容创作，距离一次成型还有多远？
本文字数：3509 字
阅读完需：约 12 分钟
AI视频生成存在“抽卡式”反复尝试现象，单部短漫剧平均需10次生成才得一版满意结果；电商等场景更要求批量生成中商品特征（形状、颜色、标识）的高保真与强一致性。
AI生成效率提升未同步降低创作者筛选与返工成本；多模态内容需兼顾单次质量与跨批次一致性；电商等垂类对可控性、可复现性提出刚性需求。
适合AI应用工程师、多模态算法工程师、内容生产平台架构师阅读。
作者｜林绮蓓
编辑｜蔡芳芳
用 AI 生成一段视频，可能只需要几分钟。但要让它真正符合创作者的要求，往往还得一遍遍地尝试。在 AI 视频制作中，这种反复生成、筛选的过程被形象地称为 “抽卡” 。
腾讯云 WAND 多模态应用负责人朱琳在采访中提到：按照行业经验，制作一部 AI 短漫剧，从分镜到成片，过程中可能需要大约十次生成尝试，才能得到一次满意的效果。这种落差并不仅仅发生在视频领域，它揭示了当下 AI 创作中统一的现实矛盾： AI 生成内容的速度越来越快，创作者却未必能同样快速地获得自己真正

stories.title: NYT Cooking 的 AI 助手救了我工作日晚上那道鸡肉，却差点毁了蛋糕 / NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake

sources.title: NYT Cooking 的 AI 助手救了我工作日晚上那道鸡肉，却差点毁了蛋糕 / NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
sources.title_zh: NYT Cooking 的 AI 助手救了我工作日晚上那道鸡肉，却差点毁了蛋糕
sources.title_en: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
sources.title_original: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
sources.recommend_reason_zh: NYT Cooking的AI助手实测：处理鸡肉、halibut和Bundt cake的食材替换与缩放，虽几乎让蛋糕少放一半黄油，但能基于用户评论给建议且不改原食谱。

en.reason: Testing NYT Cooking’s AI assistant on chicken, halibut, and a Bundt cake shows it handles ingredient substitutions, scaling, and equipment swaps but nearly halved the cake’s butter, while advising from user comments without changing the original recipe.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: Cognition首席安全官Alex Stamos在Decoder访谈中称，AI正让Russia、North Korea等国家行为者和小型黑客团体同时发现并利用漏洞，数十亿美元网络安全产业已难应对，我们或进入适应期的“dark age”。

en.reason: Cognition CISO Alex Stamos warns in a Decoder interview that AI lets Russia, North Korea and small hacker groups find and exploit vulnerabilities while a multi-billion-dollar cybersecurity industry lags, risking a “dark age” adaptation period.

en.title: Microsoft Research disbands its AI Frontiers team
en.reason: Microsoft Research’s roughly 50-person AI Frontiers team, founded in 2023 and behind Autogen and Fara, was folded into Microsoft AI in September 2024 and then disbanded over a clash with ex-Inflection leadership prioritizing scaling over research.

en.reason: Microsoft Research's roughly 50-person AI Frontiers group, created in 2023 to pursue Autogen and Fara agent work, ended after being folded into Microsoft AI in early September, where its approach clashed with ex-Inflection's scaling-only route.

en.title: Microsoft Research disbands its AI Frontiers team
en.reason: Microsoft Research’s roughly 50-person AI Frontiers team, founded in 2023 and behind Autogen and Fara, was folded into Microsoft AI in September 2024 and then disbanded over a clash with ex-Inflection leadership prioritizing scaling over research.

en.title: 12 Advanced UI Interaction Effects and Their AI Prompts: A Lesson in Physicality, from Press Rebound to Bottom Drawers
en.summary:
12 Advanced UI Interaction Effects and Their AI Prompts: A Physics-Feel Tutorial from Press Rebound to Bottom Sheets

Key takeaway: The difference between advanced and ordinary UI interactions essentially comes down to whether they feel physical. Advanced interactions mimic real-world mechanics—rebound, elasticity, friction, inertia—while ordinary interactions just change mechanically. If you ask AI to make a button and add an animation, it will only give you a basic scale effect. But if you name the specific interaction—press rebound, elastic toggle, ripple that follows your finger, liquid slider, card stacking—AI can reproduce it precisely. This article breaks down the visual characteristics and one-sentence AI prompts for 12 advanced interactions, with a runnable demo. The column covered overall design principles in Advanced UI Design Techniques: 7 Core Principles for Making Interfaces Feel More Premium; this article focuses on the narrower dimension of interaction motion.

1. Interactions 1–2: Press-rebound button + elastic toggle
en.reason: Twelve advanced UI interactions—a press-rebound button that springs to 1.05 before settling, an elastic switch whose dot stretches into a capsule, ripples spreading from the touch point—each get a one-line AI prompt and runnable demo.

en.title: 12 Advanced UI Interaction Effects and Their AI Prompts: A Lesson in Physicality, from Press Rebound to Bottom Drawers
en.summary:
12 Advanced UI Interaction Effects and Their AI Prompts: A Physics-Feel Tutorial from Press Rebound to Bottom Sheets

Key takeaway: The difference between advanced and ordinary UI interactions essentially comes down to whether they feel physical. Advanced interactions mimic real-world mechanics—rebound, elasticity, friction, inertia—while ordinary interactions just change mechanically. If you ask AI to make a button and add an animation, it will only give you a basic scale effect. But if you name the specific interaction—press rebound, elastic toggle, ripple that follows your finger, liquid slider, card stacking—AI can reproduce it precisely. This article breaks down the visual characteristics and one-sentence AI prompts for 12 advanced interactions, with a runnable demo. The column covered overall design principles in Advanced UI Design Techniques: 7 Core Principles for Making Interfaces Feel More Premium; this article focuses on the narrower dimension of interaction motion.

1. Interactions 1–2: Press-rebound button + elastic toggle

en.title: 212 requests, 220,000 lines of code: 19 days of an Agent taking over an open-source project
en.summary:
212 Requests, 220,000 Lines of Code: 19 Days of an Agent Taking Over an Open Source Project

**Munk AI** is a Harness Runtime for multi-agent collaboration (`The harness runtime for multi-agent collaboration`). It organizes multiple "expert Agents" into a team that runs autonomously on AI: you make only the key decisions, while Munk builds the product end to end and keeps it running.

To put the system through its paces in real-world conditions, over the past **19 days** I tried a public build approach — letting it take full control of an open source desktop app and iterate on it autonomously: **[OpenCompare](https://link.juejin.cn/?target=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fchaxiu%2FOpenCompare "https://github.com/chaxiu/OpenCompare")** (a free, open source file and directory comparison tool).

*   **212 requirements closed out**: 213 accepted in total
en.reason: Over 19 days, Munk AI's 24-agent team took over open-source file comparison tool OpenCompare, closing 212 requests, committing 227,000 lines of code and shipping 24 releases with just 20 human exchanges.

en.title: Gemini 4 Carbon tops the Intelligence Index with 59 but can’t be bought: $7.76 per task, hallucination rate up from 4% to 11%
en.summary:
The top-ranked model on the leaderboard is one you can't buy right now, even if you're willing to pay.

On October 29, third-party evaluation firm Artificial Analysis put Google's Gemini 4 Carbon at the top of its Intelligence Index v5 with a score of 59, beating out Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. The news pulled 338 upvotes and 247 comments on Hacker News, but the most upvoted discussion wasn't about how powerful the model is — it was about when it would actually be made available. As with the previous generation, Argon, at launch, Carbon is currently being pushed only to select users, and there is simply no public timeline. More interesting still, the data contains a counterintuitive detail: the new model's hallucination rate rose from 4% to 11%, nearly tripling, yet that figure is still the second-lowest in the entire field. This article takes apart the official benchmark data to see what this top ranking is really worth, and what you and I should do right now.

The top-ranked model on the leaderboard is one you can't buy right now, even if you're willing to pay.

I fell into this trap myself at first. The Agent would be running along and suddenly crash; digging into the logs, `json.loads` had thrown an exception. I stared at it for ages thinking the model had gone bad, until I printed the raw output and saw the "JSON" the model was giving me looked like this:

{"city": "Beijing", "temp": 25}

Wrapped in a layer of markdown code fence. Call it wrong and the JSON inside is perfectly fine; call it right and `json.loads` hands you a `JSONDecodeError` on the spot. This "content is fine, the outer shell errors out" situation accounts for the vast majority of the bad JSON I've hit.

1. **Markdown fences**: wrapped in ````json ... ```` because the model thinks it looks nicer that way.

Published Time: 2026-11-05T12:32:03+00:00
> 「一个很快但算错的指标，没有任何价值。」
这是「一天一个开源项目」系列的**第 254 篇**。今天的项目是 NVIDIA 开源的 **Auto Ontology**。
让 Agent 去查企业数据，最常见的翻车方式不是 SQL 语法错，而是「语义错」：`revenue` 到底是含税还是不含税？`active user` 的口径是谁定的？两个系统里都叫 `customer` 的表是不是一回事？模型会自信地写出一条能跑通、数字却不对的 SQL。
Auto Ontology 的思路是在 Agent 和数据库之间加一层「上下文层」：先从元数据里自动抽出业务术语、可复用的 SQL 表达式和表间关系，再由人来测试、修正、认证，最后让 Agent 基于这些已认证的定义来回答。项目 README 把能力归为五个动词：Discover（发现）、Ground
sources.recommend_reason_zh: NVIDIA Auto Ontology 给数据 Agent 加可认证语义层：抽取术语、SQL 属性和关系，人工认证后再回答；示例收入查询返回 $588.80，覆盖度 0.5 时追问而非硬答。

en.title: One Open-Source Project a Day (No. 254): NVIDIA Auto Ontology — Giving Data Agents a Certifiable Semantic Layer, and Admitting When It Can’t Answer
en.summary:
One Open-Source Project a Day (No. 254): NVIDIA Auto Ontology — Building a "Certifiable" Semantic Layer for Data Agents, and Admitting When It Can't Answer

Published Time: 2026-11-05T12:32:03+00:00

> "A metric that is fast but wrong is worthless."

This is the 254th installment of the "One Open-Source Project a Day" series. Today's project is NVIDIA's open-source Auto Ontology.

When you let an Agent query enterprise data, the most common failure mode isn't a SQL syntax error — it's a semantic error: Is `revenue` tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive? Who defined the `active user` metric? Are the tables both called `customer` in two different systems actually the same thing? The model will confidently write SQL that runs but returns the wrong numbers.

Auto Ontology's approach is to add a "context layer" between the Agent and the database: first automatically extract business terms, reusable SQL expressions, and table relationships from metadata; then have humans test, correct, and certify them; and finally let the Agent answer based on these certified definitions. The project README groups its capabilities into five verbs: Discover, Ground

en.title: One Open-Source Project a Day (No. 254): NVIDIA Auto Ontology — Giving Data Agents a Certifiable Semantic Layer, and Admitting When It Can’t Answer
en.summary:
One Open-Source Project a Day (No. 254): NVIDIA Auto Ontology — Building a "Certifiable" Semantic Layer for Data Agents, and Admitting When It Can't Answer

Published Time: 2026-11-05T12:32:03+00:00

> "A metric that is fast but wrong is worthless."

This is the 254th installment of the "One Open-Source Project a Day" series. Today's project is NVIDIA's open-source Auto Ontology.

When you let an Agent query enterprise data, the most common failure mode isn't a SQL syntax error — it's a semantic error: Is `revenue` tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive? Who defined the `active user` metric? Are the tables both called `customer` in two different systems actually the same thing? The model will confidently write SQL that runs but returns the wrong numbers.

Auto Ontology's approach is to add a "context layer" between the Agent and the database: first automatically extract business terms, reusable SQL expressions, and table relationships from metadata; then have humans test, correct, and certify them; and finally let the Agent answer based on these certified definitions. The project README groups its capabilities into five verbs: Discover, Ground

en.title: One open-source project a day (No. 255): Mika — an AI agent inside your Android phone that operates apps and websites for you on a background virtual screen
en.summary:
Mika is an open-source AI assistant for Android: you say one sentence, and it looks at the screen, taps buttons, and types text like a human on a hidden background screen, completing tasks across apps and web pages without taking over your main screen.

"No App APIs, no per-app adaptation."

This is post 255 in the "one open-source project a day" series. Today's project is Mika, an AI agent that runs on Android phones.

There are two common ways to let AI operate your phone: rely on each app's open API (most don't have one), or write a separate integration for every app (impossible to maintain). Mika takes a third path: look at the screen, find buttons, tap, type — like a human. The README puts it as "no App API needed, no per-app integration."

It has a very practical design: tasks run on a hidden background screen, so your main screen stays free for other things. The repo was created on 2026-10-29 and currently has about 7.2k stars, growing fast — but the project is still very new. Everything below is based on the README and has not been tested one by one.

Mika is an Android AI assistant app: you give it an instruction and it executes tasks across multiple apps and web pages. The repo description is "an on-device Android AI agent that operates [it] for you
en.reason: Mika, an open-source Android AI agent with 7.2k Stars, runs tasks on a hidden background screen by tapping and typing across apps and web without per-app APIs, and can connect to Ollama or LM Studio to keep screen content local.

en.title: MaxxBench – "DeepSWE scores well. But is it real?
en.reason: MaxxBench changed 89 DeepSWE tasks with a median reference-patch increase of just 17 lines (3.5%), and Claude Opus 5.5 scored 76.4% versus Gemini 3.8 Flash's 53.4%—a 23-point gap—as models talked themselves out of following changed requirements.

sources.recommend_reason_zh: Video Rebirth 将 MiniMax-H3 压缩为 13.7B 的 HyperFlow H3 Flash，用 4-8 步和 INT8/GGUF 联合生成视频与同步立体声音频，并说明 64GB 内存 PC 用 GGUF、24GB+ RTX 且 69GiB 系统内存用 INT8。

en.reason: Video Rebirth compressed MiniMax-H3 into 13.7B HyperFlow H3 Flash, generating video and synchronized stereo audio in 4–8 steps with INT8/GGUF builds, including GGUF on 64GB-RAM PCs and INT8 on 24GB+ RTX GPUs with 69GiB system memory.

stories.title: Xcode MCP 助力运行时二进制分析

sources.title: Xcode MCP 助力运行时二进制分析
sources.title_zh: Xcode MCP 助力运行时二进制分析
sources.title_original: Xcode MCP 助力运行时二进制分析
sources.recommend_reason_zh: 文章以 EXC_BAD_ACCESS(subcode 0x1d)、栈中仅有 dispatch_source_set_timer + 36 等系统库的 Crash 为例，介绍如何通过 Xcode 的 mcpbridge 调用 LLDB，让 AI 在活动调试会话中下断点、读寄存器并批量验证，再由人收敛假设。

en.title: Xcode MCP enables runtime binary analysis
en.reason: An EXC_BAD_ACCESS crash with subcode 0x1d and a stack showing only dispatch_source_set_timer + 36 in libdispatch illustrates how Xcode's mcpbridge exposes LLDB to AI for setting breakpoints, reading registers and batch-verifying hypotheses, with engineers converging the results.
